capabilities: Track tasks with due dates, owners, effort estimates and sub-items in plain Markdown files
Lay out each day as a time-block timeline and slot tasks into calendar days
Organize projects and milestones as one Markdown file per project with ## sections
Compute team workload from person-day estimates and capacity profiles
Publish and subscribe to message feeds via vault sync or an optional local Python service
extras: Distributed via BRAT as a beta plugin; ships a sample-data generator, a Python message service, and a migration script for replacing ```tasks queries. Known limits include no drag-to-reschedule, no recurring-task parsing, and session-only read state.
problem: Obsidian has no timeline-first view that ties tasks, daily schedules, project milestones and team workload together without a side database.

relations.evidence: It coexists with obsidian-tasks, dataview, kanban, calendar and friends: TLT reads plain - [ ] lines
It coexists with obsidian-tasks, dataview, kanban, calendar and friends

requires.name: message service (services-py/tlt_service.py) or vault sync (iCloud / Dropbox / Syncthing / Git)

summary: Timeline-first workbench for tasks, calendar scheduling, project milestones, team workload and a standalone message center, all in plain Markdown.
